problem: Find the surface area of the portion of the surface $z=3\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2\sqrt{2}y$ whose projection onto the $xy$-plane is bounded by $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡2x$ and the $x$-axis from $x=0$ to $x=\frac{\pi }{2}.$

feedback.problem: Find the surface area of the portion of the surface $z=\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}$ whose projection onto the $xy$-plane is bounded by $y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}}$ and the $x$-axis from $x=-1$ to $x=1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ defined by $z=f(x,y)$ with $(x,y)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

In this case, our surface is given by

$$
z=\frac{{x}^{2}}{2},\,(x,y)\in D
$$

where the region $D$ is given by

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le \frac{1}{\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14066535/assets/b9504140a4827cd74b74e8c23f76e1305389f1bc93a87834a37d4b20222e56f0.png)

Now, since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂z}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})=x, \\ \frac{∂z}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2})=0,\end{aligned}
$$

the surface area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+(x)^{2}+(0)^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1/\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}}\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}\cdot y\,{|}_{0}^{1/\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\,{|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =1-(-1) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
